title: Church History I: The Apostolic Era to 1500
description: The story of the church from Pentecost to the eve of the Reformation. Students meet the Apostolic Fathers, the apologists and martyrs, the great councils and creeds, the Cappadocians and Augustine, the rise of monasticism, the missions to Europe, the East-West schism, the medieval papacy, scholasticism, and the late-medieval reform movements. Throughout, students read primary sources from the library and ask how the church's history shapes its faith and practice today.

quiz_bank.question: Summarize the Pelagian controversy.
quiz_bank.answer_key: Pelagius taught that humans are born without original sin and can obey God by free will aided by external grace (law, example); Augustine argued that since the fall all are born in sin and need God's inner, prevenient and effective grace to will and do good; councils (e.g. Carthage 418) condemned Pelagianism.

quiz_bank.question: What is the main idea of the City of God?
quiz_bank.answer_key: Written after Rome's sack (410), it shows that Christianity did not cause Rome's fall; history is the story of two cities, the earthly city built on love of self and the heavenly city built on love of God, intermingled now and separated at the final judgment.

quiz_bank.question: What were the main contributions of monasticism to the church?
quiz_bank.answer_key: Preservation of Scripture and learning, models of prayer and discipleship, missionary work, care for the poor and sick, spiritual guidance, and a protest against worldliness in the imperial church.

quiz_bank.question: Summarize Gregory the Great's significance.
quiz_bank.answer_key: As pope he organized relief, strengthened the church's administration, promoted liturgy and monasticism, wrote the influential Pastoral Rule on shepherding souls, and sent Augustine of Canterbury's mission to England.

quiz_bank.answer_key: Within a century Islam conquered much of the Christian Middle East, North Africa and Spain; ancient churches became minorities; Christianity's center shifted to Europe; later it contributed to the Crusades and shaped East-West relations.

Summarize Anselm's satisfaction theory.
quiz_bank.answer_key: Sin dishonors God and incurs an infinite debt humans owe but cannot pay; only God can pay it; therefore only one who is both God and man can make satisfaction; Christ freely offers his life, restoring God's honor and meriting reward given to sinners.

quiz_bank.question: How does Aquinas relate faith and reason?
quiz_bank.answer_key: Reason can demonstrate some truths about God (existence, oneness) - 'preambles of faith' - while other truths (Trinity, incarnation) are known only by revelation; grace perfects nature, faith and reason do not contradict, and theology uses reason in service of revealed truth.
